requirement: Settings › AI accounts connects Kimi, GLM and Qwen with a pasted API key: the broker proves the key on a cheap vendor door before sealing it, sorts refusals into key / plan / vendor, never keeps an unproven key, and tells the client each vendor's sign-in kind; the client draws the key row and maps the door's refusals

oracle.invariant: 0 failures. Every test named in run.tests reports ok.
oracle.productSourcesScope: file-level: the files the case imports, reads or runs (declaration line, or the first code line); the invariant is exercised through them, the executed assertion is the case command

writes: run dir under QA_ARTIFACT_ROOT: logs/, tmp/<case> (the child TMPDIR, removed after the run)

assertionIds: a good key is proven on /models and kept as a key blob with a hashed identity
a good key is proven on the quota door and kept as a key blob with a hashed identity
a rejected key is a key error
a rejected key is a key error, whether Z.ai says so in the status or only in the body
a key without a membership is a plan error, not a bad key
a key with no coding plan or balance is a plan error
a key whose account is out of quota or in arrears is a plan error
kimi down or slow is a vendor error
Z.ai down or slow is a vendor error
DashScope down or slow is a vendor error
another region is a second probe away: a Beijing key refused abroad is kept with the endpoint that took it
a key refused by both regions is a key error; any other answer is not
any 403 is an access refusal (plan), never a wrong key
